text: The Evangelical Lutheran Church in Tanzania (ELCT; Swahili: Kanisa la Kiinjili la Kilutheri Tanzania) is the federation of Lutheran churches in Tanzania and one of the largest Lutheran denominations globally, with over 6 million members, representing 13% of the Tanzanian population. It is the second largest Lutheran church in the world and the largest in East Africa. The church is led by a presiding bishop and twenty-eight diocesan bishops, representing 28 dioceses, with its head office located in Mbeya since 1967. It is affiliated with the All Africa Conference of Churches (AACC), the Christian Council of Tanzania, the Global Confessional and Missional Lutheran Forum, and the Lutheran World Federation. The ELCT offers worship, Christian education, and a range of social services, including disaster response, healthcare, and AIDS education and relief. The first Lutheran missionaries arrived in German East Africa in 1887 when the Evangelical Missionary Society for East Africa (EMS), based in Berlin, Germany, established a station at Kigamboni, Dar es Salaam. A second group of German missionaries entered via South Africa and settled in the Southern Highlands. Missions from Germany continued throughout the late 19th and early 20th centuries despite interruptions from the Hehe Wars (1891), the Maji Maji Uprising (1905–1907), World War I, and World War II. In 1938, seven Lutheran churches formed the Federation of Lutheran Churches in Tanganyika, which later merged into the Evangelical Lutheran Church in Tanzania. In 1964, Johannes Lilje, presiding bishop of the United Evangelical Lutheran Church of Germany, consecrated Stefano Moshi, elected as the first president of the new church body and a proponent of episcopacy, as the first presiding bishop of the ELCT. The church's seat is in Arusha and is primarily financed through collections, donations, and project grants from churches in the Global North. The ELCT is led by a presiding bishop, or "Mkuu," elected to four-year terms from among the bishops, and 24 bishops who oversee local dioceses; the current presiding bishop is Alex Malasusa. The church employs 1,360 ordained pastors (28 overseas), 3,000 lay evangelists, and 300 community officers (2014 figures). Women are not ordained in all dioceses, though the national church began ordaining women as of 1990; ordination remains a sensitive issue, with local dioceses making independent decisions. The ELCT is one of the fastest-growing churches globally, with an annual increase of approximately 8% in baptized members. Social services are central to its mission and include departments focused on disaster response, healthcare, and AIDS education and relief. The ELCT comprises regional dioceses in Kenya, South Sudan, Tanzania, Indonesia, Mongolia, Germany, Norway, Sweden, and Peru. Lutheranism is rooted in the theology of Martin Luther, with official confessional writings in the Book of Concord. The ELCT accepts the unaltered Augsburg Confession as a true witness to the Gospel and does not adhere to biblical inerrancy, instead supporting scholarly methods of biblical analysis, aligning with moderate Protestant traditions. Like other Lutheran bodies, the ELCT recognizes two sacraments: Communion (Eucharist) and Holy Baptism (including infant baptism); Confession and absolution is often included but is considered a return to the forgiveness of baptism, so strictly speaking, only two sacraments exist. The ELCT holds to the Lutheran doctrine of sacramental union, affirming that Christ's body and blood are truly present "in, with and under" the bread and wine, with all communicants receiving both bread and wine and the actual body and blood of Christ. This is sometimes referred to as consubstantiation, though Lutherans reject a philosophical explanation, viewing the presence as a mystery rather than a philosophical concept. This belief is more aligned with Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox traditions than with most Protestant views, which often doubt or deny the actual presence of Christ's body and blood in communion. In August 2013, the ELCT established a relationship with the North American Lutheran Church through a "Memorandum of Understanding," paving the way for full communion between the two churches.
